correctness.rationale: Conditioned uniform-forest enumeration by the matrix-tree minor gives k n^(m-1); deleting fixed r noncyclic leaves gives k(n-r)^(m-1). Dividing and summing ordered r-sets proves exact factorial moments; occupancy equivalent. The conditional mean differences are strictly signed and covariance negative by independent-copy symmetrization. Exact cyclic-core probabilities imply Rayleigh moment convergence; uniform Taylor expansion on k<=n^(3/5) with exponentially small complement controls covariance to sharp sqrt(n) coefficient. Separately enumerated all mappings up to six vertices and n=100,1000,10000 numerical asymptotics. Finite tests do not certify general proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparisons establish that cyclic-set-conditioned rooted forests are classical (Pitman; Hansen–Jaworski) and terminal/cycle marginals are classical (Flajolet–Odlyzko). The asserted exact conditional terminal count and especially the signed sharp mixed-covariance asymptotic were not identified in inspected primary passages or semantic literature searches. The same old forest theorem can indirectly yield conditional moments and historical priority remains at risk; no independence or uniqueness is claimed.
residual_risks: Rooted-forest decomposition and total forest counts are classical and are not original; a published generating function may imply the terminal conditional moments by specialization.
Mylläri 2002 entire leaf-in-forest article was unavailable after open-access/arXiv attempts; complete text was not accessible; its abstract was used only for risk assessment.
Some Russian-language historical mapping-strata works (e.g. Sachkov, Pavlov, Proskurin) could encode related mixed moments; full comparison inaccessible.
No independent external historical-priority audit performed; database semantic search absence is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: Two canonically defined random-mapping statistics have disparate scales: cyclic core is order sqrt(n), terminal count order n. Conditioning reveals a nontrivial empty-box law and strict negative regression, while first-order terminal fluctuations hide a sqrt(n)-order mixed-covariance constant. The fact explains weak correlation despite persistent negative dependence and supplies exact finite conditional laws usable for joint mapping statistics, rather than a decorative parametrization.
